answer.location_description: Small patch in the upper part of the image, right of centre, above the nodule: rows 2-4, columns 14-17. It sits within a broader pro-malignant band along the top edge.
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright spot/marker outside the nodule (artifact patch)
answer.mechanism: The structured layer-1 units 1, 2, 8, 10, 18, 20, 24 and 28 have negative biases and pro-malignant downstream weights. They carry a concentrated positive weight spot at rows 3-4, cols 14-16. The opposing units 23, 27, 29 and 31 have large positive biases and pro-benign downstream weights; they carry strong negative weights at the same pixels. Brightness there therefore drives layer-2 units u3, u10 and u12 up (output weights +65, +73, +75). It drives u1 and u13 down (output weights -99, -80), because 'benign' units 23/27/29/31 that feed them get switched off. Both effects push the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Rows 3-4, cols 14-16, malignant-side units: unit 8 has r3c15=49 and r4c16=40. Unit 10 has r3c15=43. Unit 20 has r3c14-15=35,44 and r4c16=34. Unit 24 has r3c16=48. Unit 1 has r3c16=47. Unit 2 has r4c16=45. Unit 18 has r3c16=46. Unit 28 has r4c15=43. Same pixels, benign-side units: unit 27 has r3c15-16=-40,-49 and r4c15=-35. Unit 29 has r3c14=-34 and r3c16=-41. Unit 23 has r4c16=-36. Unit 31 has r4c16=-31. These magnitudes are as large as the units' nodule-centre weights, although they lie well outside the nodule's ~12 px extent. The adjacent rows 1-2 carry much weaker weights, so the spot looks isolated. Routing in layer 2: u3 takes +43..+86 from units 1/2/8/10/20/28 and -65/-75 from units 23/27. u10 and u12 show similar patterns. u1 and u13 take strongly negative weights from units 18/20/24 and positive weights from units 23/29/31 or 27/29. Caveat: these units also weight the whole border, with similar hotspots at the bottom-left (rows 18-21, cols 0-2) and the top-right top row. So the patch could partly be part of a generic 'bright surroundings' feature, which lowers my confidence.
answer.main_feature: A few structured first-layer detectors compare the nodule interior and margin with its surroundings. Center-weighted units 23/27/29/31 favour a compact, well-defined nodule and push toward benign. Units 1/2/8/10/18/20/24/28 respond to irregular or spiculated margins and bright surrounding structure and push toward malignant.
